nodes.text: Watch your step — shavings underfoot. Take your time, look at the benches. You'll want either a door or a lesson. I stock both.
Speak up over the benches. What'll it be?

Everything the mountain can't smelt. Doors, carts, cradles, coffins — the honest procession of a life, all off these benches. The saw yard breaks the pine down, my hall joins it back up, Dagny bends the offcuts into barrels and Haki flights the straightest of it. One tree, four trades. That's the Timberway: nothing wasted but the bark, and Wyn takes the bark.

The great doors, the moot dais, and the Queen's window box — the window box was hardest, because Her Majesty knows joinery, and *checked*. The King thanked me for the dais. The doors thank me every winter by not warping. That's worth more.

The patterns on my counter will start you: measures, joints, which grain forgives and which doesn't. After that it's ten thousand shavings, and a temper you learn to lose quietly. Take the wood at its own pace and it behaves forever. Same with apprentices. Tilo down at the ford was mine — look at him now.
Patterns, schematics, and the measures I trust. Priced fair. Learn them slower than you want to.
True grain. And check your ladder rungs — that's free.
